tiers.B: image artefact, label correct: kept (labels cut at cutoff_h)

timeline_rule: out-of-fold fit lowers phase error by >= 0.3 and to <= 60 %, slope inside grid; disagreements with the file signature decided by inspection
inspected_by: AI-assisted inspection: a vision-capable language model under the authors' direction; not an embryologist

timeline_mismatch.description: The images run on a different clock from the annotation: pairing the k-th image with annotation frame k lets the label drift, by up to tens of hours by the end of the video.

no_division.description: The embryo stays a single cell and never divides, while the annotation records divisions.

blank_throughout.description: Every frame is a featureless bright well; no embryo is visible.

annotation_ahead.description: The annotated onsets run ahead of what the images show, by one to two division stages.

embryo_removed.description: The well empties partway through the recording (removal for transfer or freezing, or hatching out of view) and the release extends the last annotated phase to the end.

dark_frames.description: Frames in the middle of the recording are under-exposed to near black.

abrupt_cleavage.description: Direct cleavage from one cell to three or more, or to a fragmented mass, within minutes.

heavy_fragmentation.description: Heavy fragmentation makes the cell count, and so the stage, hard to read.

annotation_behind.description: Annotated onsets run several hours behind what the images show.

annotation_truncated.description: The annotation stops at one phase and holds it to the end while the embryo develops further; labels are cut where the images leave that phase.

developmental_arrest.description: The embryo arrests and degenerates; the last annotated phase is held to the end.
